subject: Saturation signals & graceful degradation playbook for private GPU pools

Subject: Saturation signals & graceful degradation playbook for private GPU pools

Team —

We're prepping the playbook for private GPU pools (VPC/edge on-prem placements) to handle saturation events and ensure predictable customer-facing SLOs without cascading failures. Goal: define clear signal thresholds, immediate mitigations, and a runbook for rolling graceful degradation (model fallback, admission control, cache warmup) so on-call can execute reliably.

Outline / asks:
- Propose 3 primary saturation signals (GPU util, queue length, token/sec) and conservative numeric thresholds for initial runbook.
- Define staged actions (soft-throttle, per-tenant admission, model downgrade to quantized variant, route to alternate region).
- Network failure / egress-constrained scenarios: ensure we have per-tenant egress caps and a warmup strategy for KV cache to avoid cold-burst latency spikes.
- Impact surface: latency/p95 targets, billing/usage transparency for customers during fallback, and metrics to drive alerts & auto-ops.

I've attached a starting spec for saturation metrics (saturation-metrics-spec.xlsx). Please reply with thresholds you think are safe for a first cut and any operational gotchas from networking or infra.

Thanks — I'll collate and push a draft runbook by EOD.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Private Deployments

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-05-14T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Saturation signals & graceful degradation playbook for private GPU pools

Thanks Jonas — quick thoughts from infra/network: 

- Signal candidates (my priority order):
  * sustained GPU util > 82% for >= 5m per-GPU (accounts for transient spikes)
  * request queue length > 150 pending requests across the pool for > 3m
  * token/sec per-GPU drops (indicates small-batch latency spikes) or sudden increase in average batch size variance
  * p95 latency > 350ms for completion routes (business routes differ)

- Network considerations: many private deployments impose egress caps. When egress throttles spike, we often see long tail SLO violations even when GPUs are not fully saturated. Suggest adding a parallel egress saturation signal (bytes/sec per-host relative to contract cap). See attached matrix with customer egress tiers (network-egress-matrix.pdf).

- Fallback ordering suggestion:
  1) Soft-throttle (reject with 429 + Retry-After short window) for low-priority tenants
  2) Model downgrade to quantized variant with same logits ordering (vX -> vX-q4)
  3) Reduce max tokens for streaming-heavy routes (to preserve throughput)
  4) Route to Dedicated capacity (if customer has bill/contract) or queued-backpressure with informative billing flag

Edge case: cache warmup — if we immediately downgrade models, KV caches are incompatible across quantization in some builds; include cache-migration or parallel warm-up step in runbook.

Adding Dev to get the concrete action steps + automated policies.

— Laura

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Saturation signals & graceful degradation playbook for private GPU pools

+1 to Laura's signals. Draft runbook attached (graceful-deg-runbook.md) and a sample autoscaler snippet (autoscale-policy.yaml). Key technical thresholds & actions I recommend for a first-pass, tuned to common private pool profiles: 

Saturation signals (trigger window = sliding 5m unless noted):
- GPU_util_pct >= 82% for >= 5m -> PRIMARY
- request_queue_length >= 150 -> PRIMARY
- p95_latency >= 350ms for completion endpoints -> PRIMARY
- token_rate_per_gpu drops > 30% relative to baseline for >= 3m -> SECONDARY (indicates batch breakdown)
- egress_percent_of_contract >= 90% for >= 10m -> SECONDARY (network saturated)

Automated staged actions (ordered, idempotent):
1) Evaluate per-tenant priority map; apply soft-throttle to low-priority tenants (reject 15% of requests) and produce a metric: throttled_requests_count.
2) Increase target replicas (scale-out) with aggressive warmup window: pre-warm KV caches by replaying hot prefixes for 60s on new nodes (avoid cold-start tail).
3) If scale-out cannot complete within 90s (or queue remains > 200), perform model downgrade: switch routing policy from model:vX -> model:vX-quantized with same tokenization. Maintain a tagged fallback in the audit trail.
4) If degradation persists after model downgrade for 5m, enable degradation-route: stream-lite (reduced max_tokens, prioritized top-k sampling) for best-effort tenants.
5) Final action: queue requests with estimated ETA and send tenant notification webhook; escalate to oncall SRE.

Operational caveats:
- Cache incompatibility: when moving between float32 and q4 variants, KV cache keys are not portable. We must warm new variant caches by replaying recent prefixes (this is in runbook).
- Billing transparency: annotate requests with fallback_code so downstream billing can apply discounted rates.
- Observability: expose derived metrics: pool_headroom_pct, effective_batch_size, cold_start_rate, fallback_rate by tenant. Add dashboard rows and alert thresholds (included in attachment).

Attaching runbook + policy. I'll mock up Grafana panels and add alert playbooks to INF-2158.

— Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Hi team — thanks for the rapid turnaround. A few customer-side constraints and asks from AcmeCloud: 

- Billing: we need clear rules for when a fallback/DG (degraded) mode is used vs normal serving. If you switch us to a quantized model mid-request, we need both a delta in cost and an SLA note. Can you expose a flag in the usage export?
- Latency tolerance: for our product the p95 must remain < 400ms for auth-heavy routes; anything above that requires a degraded-mode notification to our SREs.
- Network: in our private deployments we see egress throttling at the node-level during heavy batched uploads; if fallback requires extra network to warm caches it may worsen the case. Any way to perform local cache warmup without egress?

If you can confirm the fallback metric annotations and a sample billing event payload (even if draft) that will let us sign off on the acceptance testing.

— Emily Clark
SRE Lead, AcmeCloud
